plainName: Deductions against income from other sources
summary: Some expenses are deducted from income from other sources: a banker's commission for collecting interest on securities, other spending laid out only to earn the income, a share of a family pension, half the interest on compensation, and all of a fund pension's commutation or a government gratuity paid on a death. Against dividends, only interest on money borrowed for them, and only in the years and within the limit the law allows.

routes.name: Banker's commission
routes.description: Commission paid to collect interest on securities.

routes.description: Spending laid out wholly and only to earn the income.

routes.name: Family pension
routes.description: A share of a family pension, up to the regime's limit.

routes.name: Interest on compensation
routes.description: Half of interest received on compensation.

routes.name: Fund pension commutation and death gratuity
Interest against dividends
routes.description: Interest on money borrowed for dividends or units, within the year's limit.

disqualifiers.description: Deductions for employee contributions and for machinery let on hire are not computed here.

disqualifiers.description: A banker's commission is deducted only against interest on securities.
Nothing is deducted against a deemed dividend.
Interest payable abroad or salary payable abroad on which tax was not paid or deducted is not deducted.
